questions.question: In a canonical simplex tableau for a maximization LP, the objective row is written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$. Which variable does the entering variable rule select?
options: A nonbasic variable with the most negative $q_j$
A nonbasic variable with the largest positive $q_j$
A nonbasic variable with the $q_j$ closest to zero
A basic variable with the most negative $q_j$

questions.question: For a maximization LP whose canonical tableau has objective row written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$, why does a more negative $q_j$ make the nonbasic variable $x_j$ more attractive to enter?
options: It means $x_j$ can be raised further before stopping
It means a higher increase of $z$ per unit of $x_j$
It means $x_j$ uses fewer resources per unit
It means $x_j$ has the largest original profit

questions.question: In a canonical maximization tableau with objective row written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$, both $q_1=-5$ and $q_2=-2$ are negative and $x_1,x_2$ are nonbasic. The rule selects $x_1$. What would raising $x_2$ instead do, per unit, with the other nonbasic variables at $0$?
options: Lower $z$ by $2$ per unit, since the rule rejected it
Leave $z$ unchanged, as only $x_1$ is allowed to move
Raise $z$ by $2$ per unit, also an improvement
Raise $z$ by $5$ per unit, the same as for $x_1$

questions.question: In a canonical maximization tableau with objective row written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$, the nonbasic variables $x_2$ and $x_4$ both have the most negative coefficient $-4$. Which choice does the entering variable rule allow?
options: Only $x_2$, the smaller index
Either $x_2$ or $x_4$ may enter
Both enter in the same iteration
Neither, since a tie means optimal

questions.question: In a canonical maximization tableau with objective row written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$, the nonbasic variable $x_3$ has $q_3=0$. What does raising $x_3$ alone do to $z$, and is $x_3$ an improving candidate?
options: $z$ rises; $0$ is the smallest value, so $x_3$ is the best
$z$ stays the same; $x_3$ is not an improving candidate
$z$ falls; zero coefficients mark worsening variables
$z$ stays the same; $x_3$ must enter as it is nonbasic

questions.question: A maximization LP has initial objective row $z-4x_1-6x_2-x_3=0$, with $x_1,x_2,x_3$ nonbasic and the slacks basic. Which variable enters by the entering variable rule?
options: $x_2$, the most negative coefficient
$x_1$, the first nonbasic variable
$x_3$, the coefficient nearest zero
None, since every $q_j$ is negative

questions.question: A canonical maximization tableau has objective row $z+4x_1-3x_3+s_1-2s_2=18$, where $x_1,x_3,s_1,s_2$ are nonbasic. Which variable enters by the entering variable rule?

During simplex on a maximization LP, the current canonical tableau shows the objective row $z-\frac{2}{3}x_1-\frac{3}{4}s_2+\frac{1}{2}s_1=8$; the nonbasic variables are $x_1,s_1,s_2$. Which of them should enter next?
options: $s_1$, as $\frac{1}{2}$ is the smallest
$x_1$ or $s_2$, as both are negative

questions.question: The LP $\max\ 2x_1-x_2+3x_3$ subject to $\le$ constraints is started with the slacks as basic variables and objective row written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$. Which variable enters first?
options: $x_2$, objective coefficient $-1$
$x_1$, row coefficient $-2$
$x_1$ or $x_3$, both negative
$x_3$, row coefficient $-3$

questions.question: A canonical maximization tableau has objective row $z-3x_1-2x_2=6$ with $x_1,x_2$ nonbasic. The entering variable is raised from $0$ to $2$ while the other nonbasic variable stays $0$. What is the new value of $z$?

The objective row $z-3x_1-x_2=0$ of a maximization LP is kept unchanged after $x_1$ has been made basic. Why must this row first be rewritten in canonical form before the entering variable rule is applied?
options: The rule may only be applied when the right-hand side is $0$
The rule must ignore $x_1$, but $-3$ would still be selected
Basic $x_1$ appears in it, so its coefficients are not net rates
Canonical form is needed to make every coefficient negative first

questions.question: For $\max\ 4x_1+3x_2$ with $2x_1+x_2+s_1=8$, the canonical tableau with $x_1$ basic has objective row $z-x_2+2s_1=16$. Why is the improvement rate of $x_2$ only $1$, although its profit is $3$ per unit?
options: The rate is $3$; the row coefficient is just written in other units
Raising $x_2$ forces $x_1$ down, losing $2$ of profit per unit
$x_2$ must enter at rate $1$ because $s_1$ stays basic
Profit $3$ minus the coefficient $2$ of $s_1$ gives $1$

questions.question: A feasible canonical tableau of a maximization LP has objective row $z+\frac{3}{2}s_1+\frac{1}{2}s_2=9$, where $s_1,s_2$ are the nonbasic variables. What does the entering variable rule give here?
options: $s_2$, as it has the smallest positive coefficient
$s_1$, as it has the largest coefficient in the objective row
None; with all $q_j\ge0$ the solution is already optimal
A basic variable, as no nonbasic one has $q_j<0$

questions.question: A canonical maximization tableau has objective row $z-3x_1-2x_2=0$. Feasibility allows raising $x_1$ alone to at most $2$, or $x_2$ alone to at most $5$. Which variable does the rule select, and what is the resulting gain in $z$?
options: $x_2$, since its total gain of $10$ is larger
$x_1$, with gain $10$, the larger of the two possible gains
$x_1$, with gain $3$, the size of its coefficient
$x_1$, with gain $6$, although $x_2$ would give $10$

questions.question: For $\max\ 3x_1+x_2$ with $x_1+x_2+s_1=4$ and $x_1+3x_2+s_2=7$, a tableau has basic variables $x_1,s_2$ but still uses the objective row $z-3x_1-x_2=0$. Which variable should enter by the entering variable rule?
options: $x_1$, since $-3$ is the most negative coefficient in the row
$x_2$, as its $-1$ is the only negative nonbasic coefficient
None, since the canonical row $z+2x_2+3s_1=12$ has no $q_j<0$
$s_1$, because its coefficient $0$ is the smallest available

questions.question: To minimize the cost $2x_1-5x_2+x_3$ under $\le$ constraints, the simplex method is run on $\max\ z=-2x_1+5x_2-x_3$ from the slack basis, objective row written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$. Which variable enters first?
options: $x_1$, the most positive coefficient
$x_3$, row coefficient $+1$
None, as cost cannot drop below $0$
$x_2$, row coefficient $-5$

questions.question: In a canonical maximization tableau with objective row written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$, every basic variable has coefficient $0$. A student argues that some basic variable, if increased, would still raise $z$ and should be allowed to enter. Why does the rule consider only nonbasic variables?
options: Basic variables have $q_j=0$, so increasing them can never change $z$
Basic variables are already at their upper bounds and cannot rise
Only decision variables may enter, and basic ones are slacks
Basic values follow from the nonbasic ones, so moves start there

questions.question: For $\max\ 3x_1+2.9x_2$ subject to $2x_1+x_2\le10$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the rule lets $x_1$ enter first from $z-3x_1-2.9x_2=0$. What can be said about $x_1$ at the optimal solution?
options: $x_1>0$, since the rule always picks a variable of the optimum
$x_1=5$, because the first step already reaches $(5,0)$
$x_1=0$: the optimum is $(0,10)$ with value $29$
$x_1=5$ and $x_2=10$, combining both best moves

questions.question: A maximization LP has initial objective row $z-3x_1-2x_2=0$. The variable $x_2$ is re-expressed as $x_2=2y_2$ ($y_2$ counts pairs of units). Which variable does the entering variable rule now select?
options: $y_2$, since its coefficient becomes $-4$
$x_1$, since rescaling cannot change the rule
$x_1$, since $y_2$ gets coefficient $-1$
$x_1$ or $y_2$, since both now have $-3$

questions.question: For $\max\ 2x_1+x_2$ with $x_1\le4$, $x_2\le3$, $x_1+x_2\le5$ and slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, a canonical tableau has rows $z-s_2+2s_3=7$, $x_2+s_2=3$, $x_1-s_2+s_3=2$, $s_1+s_2-s_3=2$. Which variable enters, and how do $x_1,x_2$ change per unit of it?
options: $s_2$; $x_2$ falls by $1$ and $x_1$ rises by $1$
None; all decision variables are basic, so stop
$s_3$; it has the largest coefficient in the row
$s_2$; $x_1$ and $x_2$ both rise by $1$
